title: All the Fullness of God
summary: God spoke with Moses face to face, yet no one can see God's face and live. It was only possible because Moses was speaking with the Son.
exhortation: "For in him all the fullness of God was pleased to dwell." This is amazing. Jesus is all the fullness of God.

It makes me think of Moses in Exodus 33. Moses says, "Please show me your glory." And God answers, "I will make all my goodness pass before you and will proclaim before you my name 'The Lord.' ... But you cannot see my face, for man shall not see me and live."

That is strange to me, because earlier in the same chapter, when Moses entered the tent, the pillar of cloud would come down and stand at the entrance, all the people would rise and worship, "Thus the Lord used to speak to Moses face to face, as a man speaks to his friend." What an amazing statement. And it seems contradictory. God spoke to Moses face to face, and then says no one can see his face and live. What does it mean?

It was only possible because Moses was talking with Jesus. Jesus has always been the fullness of God. As we sang yesterday, "In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God." If we want to see God, we look at Jesus. If we want to speak with God face to face as with a friend, it's only possible through Jesus, who is himself the fullness of God. As Jesus said to Philip in John 14:9, "Have I been with you so long, and you still do not know me, Philip? Whoever has seen me has seen the Father." So let's take some time this morning filling our view with Jesus.
prayer: Lord, we were helpless and lost in darkness. We had separated ourselves from your presence by our sin. What we needed was you, and what we had cut ourselves off from was you. And the very thing we needed would have struck us dead because of our sin.

If it weren't for you, Jesus, we would be utterly lost. Thank you for coming. Thank you for saving us and restoring us to a right relationship with you through your blood, your death and your resurrection. Fill our hearts with gratitude today. In Jesus' name, amen.
